data.outcome_summary: This OECD report presents first results from PISA 2000, assessing 15-year-olds’ reading literacy as the primary domain, with mathematical and scientific literacy also measured. The assessment uses pencil-and-paper tasks in multiple formats, with a total of seven hours of items distributed across nine assessment booklets so that each student completes a two-hour session; background questionnaires for students and principals provide contextual indicators. Results are reported as proficiency scale scores (with an OECD average anchored at 500 and standard deviation at 100) and as five proficiency levels for reading literacy, including benchmark-like interpretations (e.g., Level 1 as serious difficulties). The report emphasizes that within-country variation in performance is much larger than between-country variation, and that socioeconomic background is associated with performance, though the strength of this relationship varies across countries. It also provides policy-relevant interpretation cautions: higher country mean scores do not automatically imply more effective schools, and associations between attitudes and performance are not causal.
